title: 叶公好龙
subtitle: 真龙来做客

moral.zh: 真正的喜欢不只停在表面，还要愿意了解、尊重并接纳真实的样子。
moral.en: Real appreciation goes beyond appearances; it grows through understanding, respect, and acceptance.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻表面上很喜欢某事物，其实并不了解，也不是真的喜欢。
idiomMeaning.en: To profess a love of dragons while fearing a real one—claiming to like something without truly understanding or accepting it.

visualAnchor: Ancient Chu noble residence with carved wooden screens, muted red pillars, dragon paintings and ornaments; Lord Ye is a slender middle-aged man with a neat moustache, high scholar bun, ivory cross-collar robe, dark-jade sash and rust-red outer vest; the real dragon is long, jade-green, round-eyed, gentle and friendly, with small golden horns and no exposed fangs

pages.zh: 楚国的叶公最爱龙，屋里到处都是龙的图案。
pages.en: Lord Ye of Chu said he loved dragons. Dragon pictures filled his home.
pages.prompt: wide establishing view of Lord Ye happily arranging painted scrolls and carved dragon ornaments inside his residence

pages.zh: 杯子上有龙，墙上有龙，连衣带上也绣着龙。
pages.en: Dragons decorated his cups, walls, and even the sash around his robe.
pages.prompt: medium scene of the same Lord Ye proudly showing guests his dragon cup, wall painting and embroidered sash

pages.zh: 天上的真龙听说了，开心地乘着云来拜访他。
pages.en: A real dragon heard the news and happily rode the clouds down to visit.
pages.prompt: the same gentle jade-green dragon gliding through soft clouds toward the residence, excited to meet a friend

pages.zh: 真龙把头探到窗边，礼貌地朝叶公眨了眨眼。
pages.en: The dragon peeked politely through the window and blinked a friendly hello.
pages.prompt: the friendly dragon peeking carefully through an open lattice window while Lord Ye paints at a desk

pages.zh: 叶公吓了一跳，画笔落地，躲到了屏风后面。
pages.en: Lord Ye jumped, dropped his brush, and hurried behind a screen.
pages.prompt: Lord Ye startled but safe behind a wooden screen, fallen brush on the floor, dragon waiting quietly outside

pages.zh: 他看见真龙没有恶意，便慢慢走出来认真观察。
pages.en: Seeing that the dragon meant no harm, he slowly stepped out and looked more closely.
pages.prompt: Lord Ye cautiously emerging, noticing the dragon's kind eyes and relaxed pose, warm eye-level composition

pages.zh: 叶公明白了：只爱想象、不爱真实，正是叶公好龙。
pages.en: Lord Ye understood: loving only an idea, but not the real thing, was exactly his mistake.
pages.prompt: turning point as Lord Ye compares a flat dragon painting with the patient real dragon and realizes the difference

pages.zh: 他向真龙道歉，也学会先了解，再说自己真正喜欢。
pages.en: He apologized and learned to understand something before saying he truly loved it.
pages.prompt: hopeful sunset farewell, Lord Ye bowing sincerely while the smiling dragon returns to the clouds

title: 自相矛盾
subtitle: 矛和盾的难题

moral.zh: 说话要符合事实，也要前后一致；发现矛盾时，诚实改正并不丢脸。
moral.en: Speak truthfully and consistently. There is no shame in correcting a contradiction.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻自己的言语或做法前后冲突，不能同时成立。
idiomMeaning.en: Literally, one's own spear against one's own shield; it describes words or actions that contradict each other.

visualAnchor: Busy ancient Chu market with cloth awnings and wooden stalls; the merchant is a sturdy clean-shaven man with thick brows, a low topknot, ochre robe, teal sash and brown trousers; his fixed wares are one bronze-tipped spear lying safely on a red cloth and one round dark-bronze shield with a cloud pattern

pages.zh: 楚国集市上，一位商人摆出一支矛和一面盾。
pages.en: At a market in Chu, a merchant displayed a spear and a shield.
pages.prompt: wide establishing market scene, merchant beside the spear and shield laid safely across his stall

pages.zh: 他举起盾说：“我的盾最坚固，什么也刺不穿！”
pages.en: He lifted the shield. “Nothing in the world can pierce this!”
pages.prompt: merchant proudly holding the shield in front of his body while the spear remains flat on the stall

pages.zh: 他又指着矛说：“我的矛最锋利，什么都能刺穿！”
pages.en: Then he pointed to the spear. “This can pierce anything at all!”
pages.prompt: merchant gesturing proudly toward the spear lying sideways, curious shoppers listening

pages.zh: 一个孩子问：“用你的矛刺你的盾，会怎么样呢？”
pages.en: A child asked, “What happens if your spear meets your shield?”
pages.prompt: thoughtful child asking a question while pointing separately toward the safely displayed spear and shield

pages.zh: 商人张了张嘴，却发现两句话不能同时都对。
pages.en: The merchant opened his mouth, then saw that both claims could not be true.
pages.prompt: merchant pausing with a surprised thoughtful face as the market grows quietly attentive

pages.zh: 他放下盾，重新说明它们各自真正的长处。
pages.en: He set the shield down and described each item's real strengths instead.
pages.prompt: merchant calmly placing the shield beside the spear and explaining honestly to the gathered families

pages.zh: 他笑着承认：“刚才的话自相矛盾，我说过头啦！”
pages.en: He smiled. “My words contradicted each other. I exaggerated.”
pages.prompt: turning point, merchant smiling modestly with open hands, shoppers responding warmly

pages.zh: 从此，他诚实介绍货物，大家反而更愿意相信他。
pages.en: From then on, his honest descriptions made customers trust him more.
pages.prompt: hopeful closing market scene with merchant helping a customer examine the shield safely on the stall

title: 滥竽充数
subtitle: 不会吹竽的乐手

moral.zh: 混在人群里假装会做，终究不能长久；诚实学习，才能获得真正的本领。
moral.en: Pretending in a crowd cannot last. Honest practice is how real ability grows.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻没有真本领的人混在行家中充数，也可指拿不好的东西凑数。
idiomMeaning.en: To fill a place in the ensemble without knowing how to play—passing as qualified or adding inferior work merely to make up the numbers.

visualAnchor: Ancient Qi palace music courtyard with cream stone floor and vermilion columns; Mr. Nanguo is a slim man with an oval clean-shaven face, small high bun, moss-green robe, beige sash and dark trousers; the fixed yu is a traditional bundled bamboo reed instrument with a small wooden wind chamber; all musicians are calm and child-friendly

pages.zh: 齐宣王爱听大合奏，常召许多乐师一起吹竽。
pages.en: King Xuan of Qi loved hearing a great ensemble of yu players.
pages.prompt: wide establishing palace courtyard with a seated ensemble holding traditional bundled bamboo yu instruments

pages.zh: 南郭先生不会吹竽，却悄悄站进了队伍后排。
pages.en: Mr. Nanguo could not play, but he quietly slipped into the back row.
pages.prompt: Mr. Nanguo entering the back row with an uncertain smile and holding his yu awkwardly

pages.zh: 大家吹奏时，他鼓着腮帮，装作十分投入。
pages.en: When everyone played, he puffed his cheeks and pretended to join in.
pages.prompt: ensemble performing while Mr. Nanguo imitates the others without covering the instrument holes correctly

pages.zh: 合奏声很响，没人发现他一个音也没有吹出来。
pages.en: The full ensemble was so loud that no one noticed his silence.
pages.prompt: medium-wide view of layered musicians, Mr. Nanguo hidden among them and glancing sideways uneasily

pages.zh: 后来，新国君想听每位乐师一个个独奏。
pages.en: Later, the new ruler asked to hear every musician play alone.
pages.prompt: palace steward kindly arranging one chair for solo performances as musicians prepare in a line

pages.zh: 轮到南郭先生时，他低下头，再也装不下去了。
pages.en: When his turn came, Mr. Nanguo lowered his head. He could pretend no longer.
pages.prompt: Mr. Nanguo standing beside the solo chair, holding the yu quietly with a worried but safe expression

pages.zh: 他承认自己一直滥竽充数，请老乐师教他真本领。
pages.en: He admitted he had only filled a place and asked an elder musician to teach him.
pages.prompt: turning point, Mr. Nanguo bowing honestly to a kind elderly yu teacher

pages.zh: 他从一个长音练起，终于吹出了自己的第一支曲子。
pages.en: Starting with one long note, he finally learned to play a tune of his own.
pages.prompt: hopeful garden practice at sunrise, teacher listening as Mr. Nanguo plays one steady note with correct posture

title: 买椟还珠
subtitle: 漂亮盒子里的珍珠

moral.zh: 外表可以吸引目光，但判断价值时，也要看清里面真正重要的东西。
moral.en: A beautiful appearance may catch the eye, but wise choices also consider what truly matters inside.

idiomMeaning.zh: 买下装珍珠的木匣，却退还珍珠；比喻取舍不当，只重外表而忽略本质。
idiomMeaning.en: To buy the box and return the pearl—valuing attractive packaging while overlooking what is truly precious.

visualAnchor: Ancient Zheng market with warm wooden stalls; the Chu merchant is a careful middle-aged craftsman in a navy robe and rust-red sash; the buyer is a cheerful young man in a pale-ochre robe and teal belt; the fixed treasure is one round ivory pearl inside a small dark-red carved wooden box lined with cream silk, decorated with simple gold cloud motifs and no writing

pages.zh: 楚国商人有一颗温润的珍珠，准备带到郑国出售。
pages.en: A merchant from Chu took a lustrous pearl to sell in Zheng.
pages.prompt: wide establishing workshop scene, merchant carefully holding the single pearl beside simple carving tools

pages.zh: 他做了精美木匣，还铺上香软的丝绸。
pages.en: He carved a beautiful box and lined it with soft, fragrant silk.
pages.prompt: merchant placing cream silk inside the fixed carved red wooden box, pearl waiting beside it

pages.zh: 到了集市，木匣闪闪发亮，引来许多人围观。
pages.en: At the market, the gleaming box drew a curious crowd.
pages.prompt: market stall with the open box and pearl centered, buyer leaning closer in delight

pages.zh: 一位客人一眼爱上木匣，立刻把它买了下来。
pages.en: One shopper fell in love with the box and bought it at once.
pages.prompt: buyer happily receiving the closed carved box with both hands as the merchant watches

pages.zh: 他打开盒子，取出珍珠，又把珍珠还给商人。
pages.en: He opened it, took out the pearl, and handed the pearl back.
pages.prompt: buyer returning the single pearl gently while keeping the box, merchant visibly puzzled

pages.zh: 商人提醒他：“木匣虽美，珍珠才是里面的宝贝。”
pages.en: The merchant said, “The box is lovely, but the pearl is the treasure inside.”
pages.prompt: merchant calmly showing the pearl beside the open box, buyer listening with dawning understanding

pages.zh: 客人明白，买椟还珠，就是只看外表、忘了真正价值。
pages.en: The buyer understood: choosing the box over the pearl meant missing the real value.
pages.prompt: turning point as buyer studies both the box's decoration and the pearl's soft glow thoughtfully

pages.zh: 他重新比较后，学会从外到里认真做选择。
pages.en: After comparing both, he learned to look beyond the surface before choosing.
pages.prompt: hopeful closing scene, buyer and merchant discussing the box and pearl together with respectful smiles

title: 南辕北辙
subtitle: 去南方却向北走

moral.zh: 能力和条件再好，也要先找准方向；方向错了，越努力可能离目标越远。
moral.en: Even strong skills and good resources need the right direction; effort on the wrong road can carry us farther from the goal.

idiomMeaning.zh: 车头向南、车辙却向北；比喻行动和目的正好相反。
idiomMeaning.en: The shafts point south while the tracks run north—actions going in the opposite direction from the intended goal.

visualAnchor: Ancient Wei countryside crossroads with a stone direction marker, rolling fields and distant hills; the traveler is a confident man with a round clean-shaven face, navy short robe, ochre sash and small topknot; his friend is lean with a sage-green robe and beige sash; fixed two-wheeled wooden carriage pulled by one calm chestnut horse with cream blaze

pages.zh: 魏国有个人准备去南方的楚国，带足行李出了门。
pages.en: A traveler from Wei packed for the southern state of Chu and set out.
pages.prompt: wide establishing crossroads, traveler loading his fixed carriage while a route map points toward southern hills

pages.zh: 可是车夫挥动缰绳，马车却沿着北边大路前进。
pages.en: But the driver guided the carriage onto the road heading north.
pages.prompt: the same carriage rolling north past the stone marker, southern hills visible behind

pages.zh: 朋友追上来提醒：“楚国在南边，你走反啦！”
pages.en: His friend caught up. “Chu is south. You are going the wrong way!”
pages.prompt: friend beside the stopped carriage pointing calmly toward the opposite southern road

pages.zh: 旅人说：“别担心，我的马跑得又快又有力。”
pages.en: “Do not worry,” said the traveler. “My horse is fast and strong.”
pages.prompt: traveler proudly patting the calm chestnut horse while his friend remains concerned

pages.zh: 他又说：“我带的钱很多，车夫的本领也特别好。”
pages.en: “I have plenty of money, and my driver is very skilled,” he added.
pages.prompt: traveler showing a tied coin pouch and gesturing toward the capable driver, all beside the carriage

pages.zh: 朋友摇头：“这些越好，只会让你更快离开楚国。”
pages.en: His friend shook his head. “Those advantages only take you away faster.”
pages.prompt: friend drawing one simple route line in dust, traveler leaning closer and beginning to understand

pages.zh: 旅人望着车辙，终于明白这正是南辕北辙。
pages.en: Looking at the tracks, the traveler finally understood that his journey opposed his goal.
pages.prompt: turning point, traveler comparing northbound wheel tracks with the southern road and stone marker

pages.zh: 他调转马车，先认准方向，再踏踏实实向南出发。
pages.en: He turned the carriage around, checked the direction, and started south.
pages.prompt: hopeful wide ending, fixed carriage now traveling toward sunlit southern hills, friend waving goodbye

title: 杯弓蛇影
subtitle: 杯子里的影子

moral.zh: 害怕时先查清事实，许多担忧会在认真观察后消失。
moral.en: When fear appears, look for the facts; careful observation can make many worries disappear.

idiomMeaning.zh: 把映在杯中的弓影误认成蛇；比喻因疑神疑鬼而产生不必要的恐惧。
idiomMeaning.en: Mistaking a bow's reflection in a cup for a snake—becoming frightened by an unfounded suspicion.

visualAnchor: Quiet Western Jin reception room with pale plaster wall, low dark-wood table, lattice window and one curved dark-red decorative bow hanging high on the wall; host Yue Guang is a calm middle-aged scholar in a deep-teal robe and cream sash; his guest is a gentle man in a rust-brown robe and jade belt; fixed small celadon cup filled with clear drink; any snake shape is only a harmless reflection, never a real animal

pages.zh: 乐广请朋友来家中小坐，两人对着清亮的杯子聊天。
pages.en: Yue Guang invited a friend to sit and talk over clear cups.
pages.prompt: wide establishing room scene with both friends at the low table, wall bow and celadon cup clearly visible

pages.zh: 朋友低头一看，杯里竟有一条弯弯的“蛇”。
pages.en: The guest looked down and saw a curved “snake” inside his cup.
pages.prompt: close over-shoulder view of the cup showing only the curved bow reflection, guest startled but safe

pages.zh: 他不敢多问，勉强喝下饮品，心里一直发慌。
pages.en: Too embarrassed to ask, he drank and carried the worry home.
pages.prompt: guest setting down the cup with an uneasy expression while the host remains unaware

pages.zh: 回家后，他越想越害怕，连饭也吃不香了。
pages.en: At home, the more he imagined, the more worried he became.
pages.prompt: guest at a simple home table, untouched bowl nearby, thinking anxiously but not ill or harmed

pages.zh: 乐广听说后，请他坐回原位，再仔细看看杯子。
pages.en: Hearing this, Yue Guang invited him back to the same seat and cup.
pages.prompt: same reception room and seating, host gently encouraging guest to inspect the cup together

pages.zh: 乐广取下墙上的弓，杯里的“蛇”立刻不见了。
pages.en: Yue Guang removed the wall bow, and the “snake” vanished at once.
pages.prompt: host safely lowering the decorative bow while guest watches the clear reflection disappear from the cup

pages.zh: 朋友恍然大悟：原来只是杯弓蛇影，并没有真蛇。
pages.en: The guest understood: it was only a bow's reflection, never a real snake.
pages.prompt: turning point, both friends comparing the bow's curve with the reflection, relieved smiles

pages.zh: 他放下担心，也记住以后先观察、再作判断。
pages.en: His worry lifted, and he remembered to investigate before deciding.
pages.prompt: warm closing tea-table scene, relaxed guest enjoying food while daylight fills the room

title: 塞翁失马
subtitle: 跑远又回来的马

moral.zh: 眼前的得失可能互相转化；遇到变化，先保持平静，再认真应对。
moral.en: Today's loss may become tomorrow's gain. Meet change calmly, then respond with care.

idiomMeaning.zh: 边塞老人丢马后反得好处；比喻坏事在一定条件下可能变成好事。
idiomMeaning.en: The frontier old man's lost horse brought unexpected good—misfortune may sometimes turn into a blessing.

visualAnchor: Ancient northern frontier village with grassy hills, low stone wall and timber cottage; the old man is lean with silver hair in a low bun, short white beard, warm brown robe and dark-teal cloak; his adult son wears a sage-green short robe; fixed family horse is light gray with dark mane, joined later by one chestnut horse; gentle rounded horses, no battle or scary imagery

pages.zh: 边塞住着一位老人，他和儿子一起照料一匹灰马。
pages.en: An old man on the frontier cared for a gray horse with his son.
pages.prompt: wide establishing cottage and pasture, father and adult son brushing the fixed gray horse

pages.zh: 一天，灰马跑过山口，不知去了哪里。
pages.en: One day, the gray horse wandered through the pass and disappeared.
pages.prompt: gray horse safely trotting toward distant grassy pass while father and son notice from afar

pages.zh: 邻居来安慰，老人却说：“这也许会带来好事。”
pages.en: Neighbors came to comfort him. “Perhaps something good may follow,” he said.
pages.prompt: neighbors gathered kindly by the empty fence, old man calm and thoughtful

pages.zh: 过了些日子，灰马带着一匹健壮的栗色马回来了。
pages.en: Days later, the gray horse returned with a strong chestnut companion.
pages.prompt: both horses entering the village together at sunrise, family and neighbors delighted

pages.zh: 儿子试骑新马时滑进草堆，脚腕需要休养。
pages.en: While trying the new horse, the son slipped into soft hay and hurt his ankle.
pages.prompt: son seated safely in a large hay pile holding his ankle, chestnut horse standing calmly nearby

pages.zh: 邻居又来叹息，老人仍说：“变化还没有结束。”
pages.en: The neighbors sighed again. The old man said, “The story is not over.”
pages.prompt: son resting comfortably on a bench with wrapped ankle, old man speaking calmly to neighbors

pages.zh: 后来青年们要远行守边，儿子因养伤留在家中。
pages.en: Later, young men left for a long frontier duty, while the son stayed home to heal.
pages.prompt: peaceful village gate, traveling group waving farewell with packs and no weapons, son resting beside father

pages.zh: 老人说：“塞翁失马，得失变化时，先平静看一看。”
pages.en: “A loss may hide a gain,” said the old man. “Stay calm as things change.”
pages.prompt: hopeful sunset pasture, healed son walking beside father and the two gentle horses

title: 闻鸡起舞
subtitle: 清晨响起的鸡鸣

moral.zh: 有目标后及时行动，坚持每天练习，才能让愿望慢慢变成本领。
moral.en: Once you have a goal, begin and practice steadily; daily effort turns wishes into ability.

idiomMeaning.zh: 听到鸡叫就起床舞剑；比喻有志向的人及时奋发、勤学苦练。
idiomMeaning.en: To rise at the rooster's call and practice sword forms—acting promptly and training diligently toward an ambition.

visualAnchor: Western Jin scholars' residence with tiled courtyard, bamboo fence and dawn mist; Zu Ti is an athletic young man with broad brows, high topknot, navy practice robe and rust sash; Liu Kun is lean with an oval face, lower bun, moss-green practice robe and beige sash; both use blunt dark-wood practice swords only, held safely and never aimed at anyone; fixed red-brown rooster with black tail feathers

pages.zh: 年轻的祖逖和刘琨住在一起，常谈自己的远大志向。
pages.en: Young Zu Ti and Liu Kun lived together and often spoke of their ambitions.
pages.prompt: wide evening study scene, the two friends reading scrolls beside the courtyard window

pages.zh: 一天清晨，天还微暗，祖逖忽然听见公鸡报晓。
pages.en: Before dawn one morning, Zu Ti heard the rooster call.
pages.prompt: dim dawn room, Zu Ti awake and listening toward the red-brown rooster outside

pages.zh: 他叫醒刘琨：“这不是坏声音，正好提醒我们练习！”
pages.en: He woke Liu Kun. “That sound is a fine reminder to practice!”
pages.prompt: Zu Ti gently waking his friend, pointing toward first light beyond the lattice window

pages.zh: 两人披衣来到院中，拿起木剑活动筋骨。
pages.en: They dressed, stepped into the courtyard, and warmed up with wooden swords.
pages.prompt: both friends stretching several steps apart, blunt wooden practice swords resting safely downward

pages.zh: 他们一招一式认真练，汗珠在晨光里闪亮。
pages.en: They practiced each careful movement as the morning light grew.
pages.prompt: coordinated flowing sword forms with wide spacing, blades never aimed at each other, sunrise behind

pages.zh: 刮风或天冷时，他们也按约定早起，不轻易停下。
pages.en: Even on cold or windy mornings, they kept their promise to rise and train.
pages.prompt: breezy autumn dawn, same friends practicing steadily as bamboo leaves move

pages.zh: 闻鸡起舞，成了他们每天把志向变成行动的办法。
pages.en: Rising at the rooster's call became their way of turning ambition into action.
pages.prompt: turning point, rooster in foreground and friends beginning practice together in golden dawn

pages.zh: 日复一日，他们更强健，也更懂得坚持的力量。
pages.en: Day by day, they grew stronger and learned the power of persistence.
pages.prompt: hopeful wide ending, friends finishing practice and bowing to each other as sun clears the roof

title: 铁杵成针
subtitle: 磨呀磨的老婆婆
origin: 宋·祝穆《方舆胜览·眉州·磨针溪》

moral.zh: 再难的事情，只要方法合适并坚持去做，也能一点点接近目标。
moral.en: Even a difficult goal comes closer when we use a sound method and keep working patiently.

idiomMeaning.zh: 把粗铁棒磨成细针；比喻只要有恒心、肯下功夫，再难的事也能成功。
idiomMeaning.en: Grinding an iron pestle into a needle—patient, persistent effort can overcome even a very difficult task.

visualAnchor: Tang-dynasty mountain village near a clear stream and stone bridge; young Li Bai is a lively 12-year-old with round face, high child topknot, pale-blue short robe, navy sash and brown trousers, carrying a cloth book bag; the elderly woman has silver hair in a low bun, warm smile, plum-brown robe and beige apron; fixed thick dark iron pestle and flat gray grinding stone, handled calmly and safely

pages.zh: 少年李白读书遇到难处，心里烦闷，便走出了学堂。
pages.en: Young Li Bai found his lessons difficult and wandered away from school.
pages.prompt: wide establishing village path, Li Bai leaving a small schoolhouse with book bag and discouraged expression

pages.zh: 溪边，一位老婆婆正拿着粗铁杵，在石头上慢慢磨。
pages.en: By the stream, an old woman slowly rubbed a thick iron pestle on a stone.
pages.prompt: Li Bai noticing the elderly woman seated safely beside the stream and grinding the fixed iron pestle

pages.zh: 李白好奇地问：“这么粗的铁杵，要磨成什么呢？”
pages.en: Li Bai asked, “What will that thick iron pestle become?”
pages.prompt: Li Bai crouching at a respectful distance, pointing curiously while the woman pauses and smiles

pages.zh: 老婆婆回答：“我要把它磨细，做成一根绣花针。”
pages.en: “I will grind it thin enough to become a sewing needle,” she replied.
pages.prompt: woman showing the thick pestle beside one tiny sewing needle held safely in a small cloth case

pages.zh: 李白惊讶：“这要磨多久？”婆婆笑着继续磨。
pages.en: “How long will that take?” Li Bai wondered. She smiled and kept going.
pages.prompt: woman resuming steady grinding, Li Bai watching the repeated careful motion with wide eyes

pages.zh: 水滴不停，铁杵一点点变细，李白也渐渐明白了。
pages.en: The stream flowed on, and the iron grew thinner little by little. Li Bai began to understand.
pages.prompt: close storytelling scene of slightly narrowed iron pestle, flowing stream and Li Bai's thoughtful face

pages.zh: 铁杵成针靠的是恒心，读书学本领也是一样。
pages.en: An iron pestle becomes a needle through persistence—and learning works the same way.
pages.prompt: turning point, Li Bai looking from the grinding stone toward his book bag with renewed determination

pages.zh: 他回到学堂，从一页读起，把难题一点点学会。
pages.en: He returned to school, began with one page, and learned step by step.
pages.prompt: hopeful classroom ending, Li Bai reading attentively by warm window light with a small confident smile

title: 胸有成竹
subtitle: 落笔前的竹林
origin: 宋·苏轼《文与可画筼筜谷偃竹记》

moral.zh: 动手之前认真观察、充分准备，心里有了清楚的图景，做事就更从容。
moral.en: Careful observation and preparation create a clear inner picture, making action calmer and more confident.

idiomMeaning.zh: 画竹前心中已有完整的竹子；比喻做事前已有成熟的考虑和把握。
idiomMeaning.en: To have the finished bamboo already in one's mind—being well prepared and confident before beginning a task.

visualAnchor: Northern Song scholar's garden and bamboo grove with gray rocks, tiled studio and soft seasonal light; painter Wen Tong is a calm slender middle-aged scholar with short neat beard, high black scholar bun, deep-teal long robe, cream inner collar and rust-red sash; fixed painting tools are a dark-wood brush, pale inkstone and vertical cream paper with no writing

pages.zh: 文同很爱竹子，常在院中的竹林旁静静观察。
pages.en: Wen Tong loved bamboo and often watched the grove in his garden.
pages.prompt: wide establishing garden scene, Wen Tong seated by bamboo with sketching tools still closed

pages.zh: 晴天，他看竹叶怎样迎着阳光舒展。
pages.en: On sunny days, he studied how bamboo leaves opened toward the light.
pages.prompt: sunlit grove, Wen Tong observing leaf angles and bright edges with focused calm

pages.zh: 风来时，他看竹竿怎样弯下，又轻轻弹回来。
pages.en: When wind came, he watched the stems bend and spring gently back.
pages.prompt: breezy bamboo grove, curved stems and moving leaves, Wen Tong studying their rhythm

pages.zh: 雨后，他还记住竹节、叶尖和深浅不同的绿色。
pages.en: After rain, he remembered every joint, leaf tip, and shade of green.
pages.prompt: fresh post-rain close scene, droplets on bamboo, Wen Tong examining joints and leaves

pages.zh: 回到书房，他闭上眼，完整的竹林已经在心里。
pages.en: Back in his studio, he closed his eyes and saw the whole grove in his mind.
pages.prompt: quiet studio, Wen Tong seated before blank paper with eyes closed, soft bamboo shadows on wall

pages.zh: 他提起毛笔，一气呵成，画出有风、有光的竹子。
pages.en: He lifted his brush and painted bamboo filled with wind and light.
pages.prompt: Wen Tong painting confident flowing bamboo strokes on vertical paper, balanced medium composition

pages.zh: 朋友赞叹：“你落笔前早已胸有成竹，难怪这样从容！”
pages.en: A friend marveled, “The bamboo was already in your mind before the brush moved!”
pages.prompt: turning point, friend admiring the finished bamboo painting while Wen Tong smiles modestly

pages.zh: 文同说：“看得认真、想得清楚，动手时自然更有把握。”
pages.en: Wen Tong said, “Observe carefully, think clearly, and your hand will know what to do.”
pages.prompt: hopeful ending, Wen Tong and friend comparing the painting with the living bamboo outside the open studio
